newsitem.title: USA: Mass. governor balks at tobacco tax subsidy plan.
newsitem.headline: Mass. governor balks at tobacco tax subsidy plan.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. William Weld is objecting to some of the details in a law, passed over his veto last July, that expands Medicaid coverage to children using a tobacco tax, according to Sunday's Boston Globe.

The measure funds the expansion of Medicaid to all children under 13 years of age in families below 200 percent of the poverty line or $31,000 for a family of four through a 25 cents a pack tax on cigarettes.

Weld, a Republican, instead will propose limiting Medicaid to children below 133 percent of the poverty line, or $21,000 for a family of four, and offering tax credits to encourage employers to cover other uninsured families, The Globe reported, citing unnamed administration sources.

A soon-to-be released study conducted by the Weld administration, projects $480 million in additional cigarette revenues over the next five years and at least $650 million in new federal money, the newspaper said.
But Democratic legislators told the Globe the governor was in for another fight on the issue.
"We'll scrutinize this very closely, but it sounds like there's a battle brewing," state Sen. Mark Montigny, who co- wrote the original law, told the newspaper.
Neither Montigny nor Weld could be reached for comment.
